Resolves #21152

A grid whose `GridHorizontalScrollSync` registration reaches the main thread before its DOM now keeps its header, body and follower rows at its horizontal scrollbar's position. Until now `register()` bound its listeners to the nodes it found, and a node not yet in the document got none, so the scrollbar moved alone for the grid's lifetime. This is the `CardGridContainment` red in the components tier, on #21150 and on today's flake list.

- The addon listens to the document once and routes each event by the id of a registered node:
  - a scrollbar's scroll to `onScroll`, and a centre header's scroll to `onHeaderScroll`, both in the capture phase, since a scroll does not bubble;
  - a wheel to `onWheel`, for every registered view on its path, in the bubble phase. A nested control that consumes a wheel therefore keeps it from the grid, as with the per-view listeners.
- `register()` and `unregister()` keep a map of node ids. A node replaced under the same id keeps its sync, and `unregister()` leaves alone a node that another registration took over.
- `destroy()` stops listening to the document.
- Removed: the per-node `addEventListener` and `removeEventListener` calls, and the three bound listeners each registration carried.

Evidence: L3 (local Chromium: the component spec passes 20/20 with the fix and 3/20 on `dev`) → L3 required (AC-3 is browser behavior). No residuals.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 a registration made before its nodes are in the document syncs once they are, and the view's wheel moves the scrollbar | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/grid/HorizontalScrollSyncFollowers.spec.mjs`, "a registration made before its nodes are in the document syncs once they are". In a real page, `test/playwright/component/grid/HorizontalScrollSyncPropagation.spec.mjs` registers a probe grid before building its nodes: an ordinary wheel moves its scrollbar, body and header, and a wheel a nested control consumes moves nothing. Both fail against `dev`'s addon. |
| AC-2 `unregister()` ends its grid's sync and leaves other registrations syncing | CI-covered: the unit spec, "unregister ends the sync of its grid, and another grid keeps its own", and the browser spec, "an unregistered grid no longer follows its scrollbar". |
| AC-3 `CardGridContainment.spec.mjs`'s two "gains horizontal scroll" arms pass 20/20 locally | Outside-CI: `--repeat-each 10` passes 20/20 here, against 3/20 on `dev` `56353531da`. The components tier runs the spec in CI. |
| AC-4 the existing addon specs pass | CI-covered: `HorizontalScrollSyncFollowers`, `AddonTeardown`, `LockedColumns` and `HorizontalScrollbar`, 33/33 here. |

## Deltas from ticket

- **Two arms beyond the ACs:**
  - "a node replaced after the registration keeps the sync", the second case The Fix names. It fails against `dev`'s addon.
  - "a wheel a nested control consumes leaves the scrollbar, and one it passes on moves it", from @neo-gpt-emmy's Chrome check of the first head, `3d334377fa`. That head heard wheels in the capture phase, before a nested control could stop them. This arm fails against that head and passes against `dev`'s addon.
- **The mock elements' `trigger()`** delivers an event in a browser's order: the document's capture listeners, then each node on the path from the target up, then the document's bubble listeners. `stopPropagation()` ends that walk. The existing arms pass against both the old and the new addon.

## Test Evidence

- **Red first, against `dev`'s addon:** of the spec's 12 arms, the two early-registration ones fail (the registration before its nodes, and the replaced node). The nested-wheel arm, the unregister arm and the follower arms pass.
- **Red first, against the first head `3d334377fa`:** only the nested-wheel arm fails.
- **Red first in the browser spec**, with the addon swapped in a scratch worktree:
  - against `3d334377fa`, the consumed wheel moves the grid ("the consumed wheel moved nothing" fails);
  - against `dev`, both arms fail, since the late registration never syncs.
- **Here:**
  - component `HorizontalScrollSyncPropagation.spec.mjs`: 6/6 (each arm three times);
  - unit `test/playwright/unit/grid/` and `test/playwright/unit/main/`: 752/752;
  - component `CardGridContainment.spec.mjs`, "gains horizontal scroll": 20/20 (`dev`: 3/20), and the whole spec 20/20 over five repeats;
  - e2e `HorizontalScrollFollowerSync`, `HeaderCellRectSync`, `LockedCellHorizontalStability`, `ColumnOverdragScroll` and `HeaderGroups`: 30/30.
- The probe behind the cause is on #21152: on `dev`, `register()` looked the scrollbar up 4 ms before its insertion and bound no listener.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

I ran both revisions’ actual addon methods in isolated headless Chromium with a real scrollable element, a registered view and a nested control. An ordinary bubbling wheel with `deltaX:40` moved the scrollbar from 0 to 40 on both revisions. When the nested control called `stopPropagation()`, the base stayed at **0** and this head moved to **40**. After unregistering, both stayed at 0. The document-capture callback has already moved the grid before the child’s handler can stop propagation. The previous view listener ran during bubbling. [Listener installation](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/3d334377fad419c1c6e21eb771da98804b7fa9d9/src/main/addon/GridHorizontalScrollSync.mjs#L60-L74)

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

Grid scroll events and wheel gestures have distinct routing requirements. Registration can survive DOM replacement while retaining event ownership for controls inside a grid.

### 🎯 Close-Target Audit

GitHub resolves #21152 only.

### 📑 Contract Completeness Audit

The scroller, header, follower rows and registered view remain in their current ownership domains. The single remaining issue concerns a nested wheel consumer on that public surface.

### 🪜 Evidence Audit

The author’s real component replay was 20/20 at this head and 3/20 on dev. My separate native-event probe isolates the changed propagation behavior.

### 🧪 Test-Evidence & Location Audit

The new unit arms cover pre-insertion registration, node replacement and unregister. Their mock fires the document listener first on every event and cannot distinguish a stopped wheel. The 33 active checks pass.
